# DepthART: A monocular depth estimation model with ~6M parameters, reproduction from CPU to edge deployment

Using an RGB image, predict the relative distance of a scene and measure its actual processing time on one's computer. This chapter reproduction **the public pre-trained model inference of DepthART MobileNetV4-M-slim-SPF**, along with local results for 224 and 448 inputs, complete performance records, and an independent-running ONNX script.

Reading prerequisites: Only understanding the Python environment and image arrays is required. For the CPU approach, there is no need for PyTorch, CUDA, TensorRT, or cameras, and no training dataset needs to be downloaded.

> The source clue is the report [ on ](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/pnSoNdPKvZxbOKBomE8QNQ). **6M refers to approximately 6 million parameters, not a 6MB file.** The actual single FP32 ONNX file downloaded in this chapter is 24,155,097 bytes, which is approximately 24.16MB / 23.04MiB. Fewer parameters can reduce deployment costs, but real-time performance depends on the operators, input size, hardware, and the entire processing chain.

## 1. What does it do in a embodied system

DepthART belongs to the visual perception front-end. It converts monocular RGB into a dense relative geometric representation, which can be used for studying scene structures, object boundaries, and visual inputs of policies. It does not directly output robotic arm actions.

```text
RGB 相机 → 图像预处理 → DepthART → 相对深度表示
                                     ↓
                           感知融合 / 规划 / 策略
                                     ↓
                              机器人控制器
```

The relative model in this chapter has no meter scale. The light and dark values in the pseudo-color map represent the internal relative predictions; the visualization is stretched to 2% to 98% of the median value of each image, so it is not possible to directly compare distances using the same color between two images. To obtain a meter output, the official metric model and the real camera internal parameters should be used, along with validation of the error in the target scene.

## 2. Why small models can still maintain generalization ability

According to [ paper ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17099) and the author's description, DepthART mainly focuses on studying the distribution of training data, distillation, and camera adaptation, rather than directly compressing the weight files of a large model into a few megabytes.

- **BRDS: Bias-resistant data sampling.** Reduces the sampling tendency in repetitive and dense regions among multi-source candidate images, enabling smaller models with limited capacity to access a more balanced visual distribution. The candidate pool reported has approximately 44 million images, and about 1.7 million images are selected after filtering.
- **Relative geometric distillation.** Uses pseudo-labels generated by Depth Anything V2-L to train small models, allowing them to learn transferable scene geometry.
- **CamFT: Camera-conditioning fine-tuning.** Protects the learned encoder representations during depth measurement, and restores absolute scale through camera adaptation and scale estimation.
- **SPF: Single-path pyramid fusion.** The subsequent MobileNetV4 approach reduces computational cost by using a cropped encoder and a lighter decoder, and uses standard ONNX operators.

This chapter only reproduces the reasoning and speed measurement of the public weights. As of 2026-10-18, the official repository still lists the complete training code and reproduction training configuration as pending release. Therefore, no BRDS distillation or CamFT training is performed here.

## 3. Which route to choose

| Route | Scale and Role | Deployment Requirements | Covered in this Chapter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TinyViM-S + DPT | Approximately 6.0M parameters, the S model from the original paper | Efficient CUDA inference and TensorRT deployment involve Selective Scan extension/plugin | Official entry provided; not run on this machine |
| MobileNetV4-M-slim-SPF | 6.054609M parameters, approximately 3.780059 GMAC at 448² | Standard ONNX operators, easy to run on CPU first | **Both 224 and 448 have been actually run** |
| TinyViM metric indoor/outdoor | Metric depth in meters based on camera perception | Corresponding domain weights, real internal parameters, and adapted preprocessing | Explanation interface; no metric evaluation in meters |

The number of parameters is based on the [ MobileNetV4 speed test table ](https://github.com/xuefeng-cvr/DepthART/blob/b307c123f19051e2d969960bba93ee3684874b90/deploy/pc/results/a6000/mobilenetv4_relative_speed.csv) released by the author along with the source code by GMAC. Standard ONNX reduces the porting barrier; the coverage, accuracy, and speed of specific NPU/BPU operators still need to be verified using the corresponding toolchains. No verification of the ROCm GPU backend is performed in this chapter.

For the 6.054609M parameter, only the parameter storage is calculated. FP32 requires approximately 24.22MB, FP16 requires approximately 12.11MB, and INT8 requires approximately 6.05MB. This is an ideal estimate; computation graph optimization, caching, and metadata will change the actual file size, and the runtime also needs to accommodate intermediate activations and the workspace. In this chapter, the official FP32 ONNX is used, and INT8 quantization is not performed.

## 4. Run on your own computer

Supporting files: [ execution script ](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/code/depthart_onnx.py), [ dependency list ](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/code/requirements.txt), [ example images ](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/assets/scene_640.webp).

The following manipulation enters the directory of this chapter first. The script only requests one of the two official model files. The first run downloads approximately 24MB and is verified by the author `CHECKSUMS.sha256`; the second run uses the cache.

### Windows / PowerShell

Execute in the root directory of the tutorial repository:

```powershell
cd '06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计'
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r code/requirements.txt

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe code/depthart_onnx.py --image assets/scene_640.webp --resolution 224 --output-dir outputs/cpu_224
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe code/depthart_onnx.py --image assets/scene_640.webp --resolution 448 --output-dir outputs/cpu_448
```

### Linux / macOS

Execute in the root directory of the tutorial repository:

```bash
cd '06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计'
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r code/requirements.txt

python code/depthart_onnx.py --image assets/scene_640.webp --resolution 224 --output-dir outputs/cpu_224
python code/depthart_onnx.py --image assets/scene_640.webp --resolution 448 --output-dir outputs/cpu_448
```

The actual validation environment for this chapter includes Windows, Python 3.12.3, ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, NumPy 2.2.6, and OpenCV 4.12.0. An environment that does not inherit system packages has been created, and after installation via `requirements.txt`, 224 offline inferences were performed, with the output meeting numerical consistency checks with the original environment. Linux/macOS commands use the same CPU API and have not been actually run on these systems; wheels matching the operating system and Python version are required during installation.

Save four files each time it runs:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `relative_prediction.npy` | Relative float32 prediction of the original image size, suitable for subsequent calculations |
| `relative_prediction.png` | Pseudo-color prediction image for easy observation |
| `comparison.png` | RGB input on the left, output of this inference on the right |
| `benchmark.json` | Model version, hash, environment, input/output shape, and sequential processing time |

Just replace `--image` to process your own images. The Chinese paths are saved by decoding and encoding file bytes; input is converted to RGB uniformly, scaled to a square, and then normalized according to the official mean and standard deviation. The output is restored to the original image size using the bilinear coordinates corresponding to `align_corners=True`. The square scaling changes the aspect ratio, and this follows the official single-image demo; it does not follow the same evaluation protocol as the dataset that preserves the aspect ratio.

The model is located in the user directory's `.cache/every-embodied/depthart/` by default, and it is not written to the tutorial repository. `--model-dir /your/model/cache` can be used to specify the existing cache, and `--offline` can be used to verify offline operation. If the cache is missing or the hash does not match, an error will be reported, and the damaged file will not be used anymore.

Formal measurement can increase the number of preheating and sampling times:

```bash
python code/depthart_onnx.py --image assets/scene_640.webp --resolution 224 --output-dir outputs/cpu_224_long --warmup 200 --samples 1000 --threads 4
```

Windows uses the above `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` to replace `python`. The number of CPU threads affects latency and resource usage; when comparing different resolutions, the same number of threads should be used to avoid interference from other computing tasks.

## 5. Actual results on this machine

The testing date is **2026-10-18 (Beijing Time)**. The device is AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, using `CPUExecutionProvider`. There are 4 internal computing threads in ONNX Runtime and 1 thread in OpenCV. Although the laptop has a NVIDIA GPU, it was not used this time. The input is a real indoor scene sample from the project page, resized to 640×427; batch=1, preheating 10 times, with 100 samples taken each time.

| Input Tensor | Model Mean / P95 | Mean with Pre/post Processing / P95 | Average Throughput Estimation with Pre/post Processing |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1×3×224×224 | 9.92 / 12.54 ms | 30.02 / 36.75 ms | 33.31 FPS |
| 1×3×448×448 | 55.30 / 82.61 ms | 81.59 / 113.92 ms | 12.26 FPS |

Original records: [224](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/evidence/benchmark_cpu_224.json), [448](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/evidence/benchmark_cpu_448.json). Each record contains 100 model execution times and 100 processing chain times, allowing for the recalculation of statistics. This belongs to single-image repeated reasoning verification with no deep true value, and thus cannot report δ1, AbsRel, or cross-scenario accuracy.

**Timing range:** “Model” refers to the synchronization `session.run` after the input tensor is ready; “With preprocessing” starts from the BGR image in memory and includes RGB conversion, scaling, normalization, inference, restoration of original image size, and quantile coloring. Both timings do not include model download, session initialization, image reading and decoding, result writing to disk, camera capture, and communication. The FPS in the table is `1000 / 平均毫秒数`, not the actual camera frame rate.

The mean processing latency for 224 is close to 30Hz, but the P95 value exceeds 33.3ms. Therefore, it is not possible to guarantee that every frame meets the 30Hz cutoff time. The results for 448 show the trade-offs between resolution, edge details, and latency. For real-time deployment of the entire system, it is also necessary to measure the latency, jitter, power consumption, and continuous performance from the camera to the consumer.

![224 Input: Left side RGB, right side local ONNX inference result](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/assets/comparison_224.png)

Figure 1: Local inference for 224 input. The relative structure of the nearby tables and chairs and the distant wall can be used to check if the model works properly; it cannot be used as a real distance annotation.

![448 Input: Left side RGB, right side local ONNX inference result ](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/assets/comparison_448.png)

Figure 2: Local inference for 448 input. Both figures are colored separately; the object contours and structures should be observed, and numerical errors cannot be compared directly using color differences.

## 6. How to verify the migration back to Jetson

The low latency figures in the article refer to NVIDIA GPUs, specified input resolution, and various inference precision levels. The desktop results of TinyViM-S, the standard ONNX results of MobileNetV4, and the CPU data in this chapter should be recorded separately. They cannot be substituted for each other, and model-only FPS should not be regarded as the closed loop control frequency for robots.

If you have a Jetson Orin NX, follow the [ official Orin NX deployment guide ](https://github.com/xuefeng-cvr/DepthART/blob/b307c123f19051e2d969960bba93ee3684874b90/deploy/orin_nx/README.md). The environment provided by the author is JetPack 6.2 and NVIDIA PyTorch 25.06 containers; for TinyViM, the Selective Scan extension and TensorRT plugins need to be built on the device, and the TensorRT engine should also be built on the target device.

It is recommended to complete the equipment acceptance in the following order:

1. Run relative depth on the same RGB image to verify shape, finite values, and visual structure; then compare the values with the official PyTorch output.
2. Fix the batch, resolution, precision, power mode, and thread configuration, and record the software version, model hash, mean, and P95.
3. Measure acquisition, preprocessing, inference, post-processing, and communication using the real camera on the device, and log frame loss and continuous operation status.
4. If reporting precision is required, evaluate according to the official dataset protocol; the relative model needs alignment with specified scales/offset, and the aligned scores cannot be used as metric errors. For MobileNetV4 on KITTI, sliding windows are also used, and a square single-image demo cannot replace it directly.

When a meter-based result is required, there is another `metric/infer_image.py` in the official interface. The internal parameter order is `fx fy cx cy`. It corresponds to the original input image and uses the appropriate indoor/outdoor checkpoint for the matching domain. Do not apply the example camera parameters to your own camera.

**Verified scope in this chapter:** download verification of two standard ONNX models, CPU single-image inference, deep image saving, and latency statistics for defined ranges. Jetson, TensorRT, NPU/BPU, meter-based measurement, training, and robot closed loop remain for subsequent independent experiments.

The model hash comes from [CHECKSUMS.sha256](https://github.com/xuefeng-cvr/DepthART/blob/b307c123f19051e2d969960bba93ee3684874b90/CHECKSUMS.sha256) submitted in the fixed source code. For the verification of post-processing coordinates and the mismatch between PyTorch bilinear interpolation, offline cache missing, and corrupted model rejection checks, see [ verification records ](../../../../06-策略抓取或抓取VLA/大模型控制、VLA、VLM/10DepthART轻量单目深度估计/evidence/validation.json).

In this chapter, the resolution is reduced to 640×427 and re-encoded; the two comparison images are the results of this chapter's execution.
